summary: Egress HTTP/2 path rewrite (percent-decoding) by corporate proxy causes presigned S3 range validation failures and corrupted shard fetches
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 403s and corrupted model shard downloads for range GETs to S3 presigned URLs when private deploy nodes fetch large model shards. Failures correlate with HTTP/2 connection coalescing through their corporate egress proxy.

Impact:
- Model shard range downloads failing or returning wrong byte ranges for BlueWave Analytics dedicated private deployment.
- Affects production inference on several services; increased errors and degraded tail latency.
- Customer experiencing inference failures for larger context requests; business impact high.

Environment:
- Private deployment in customer VPC peered via TGW, region us-west-2.
- Serving nodes use internal NLB -> egress through customer-managed proxy appliance.
- Observed on prod nodes running serving-runtime 1.9.2 and artifact-service 2.3.0.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Trigger a model request that loads >100MB of shard by-range (parallel ranged GETs).
2) Serving node opens HTTP/2 connection through corporate proxy to S3-presigned-host (us-west-2).
3) Some ranged GETs return 403 or return fewer bytes than Content-Range header implies.
4) Repeat until one of the ranges fails and inference request errors with shard checksum mismatch.

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent 403 Forbidden for signed GETs where the URL path contained encoded characters ("%2F" or query-encoded slashes introduced by range multipart assembly).
- In some successful 200 responses, Content-Length does not match expected range length; downstream checksum fails.
- tcpdump of egress shows the proxy rewriting the request-path: percent-decoding the path component before forwarding and then re-encoding differently when multiplexed on an HTTP/2 connection.

Expected behavior:
- Proxy should preserve the exact request-target used when the presigned signature was computed (canonical request). Any modification to path or percent-encoding must not alter the canonical string for S3 presigned validation.

Recent changes:
- Customer recently enabled HTTP/2 connection coalescing (single H2 connection for multiple hostnames) on their NGFW and deployed a proxy appliance firmware v5.4.

Relevant headers/log excerpts (sanitized):
- Original client request-target (from serving node): GET /model-shards/abc%2Fshard-00001?X-Amz-Algorithm=...
- Observed forwarded request-target (from proxy): GET /model-shards/abc/shard-00001?X-Amz-Algorithm=...
- S3 response: 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch (in correlated traces) or 200 with Content-Length 8191 instead of 16384 for range bytes=8192-16383.

Initial hypothesis:
- The customer egress proxy performs percent-decoding normalization when multiplexing requests across HTTP/2 streams and re-encodes using a different escaping policy, effectively breaking the presigned canonical request. For some ranges the rewriting also splits/merges path components causing range byte misalignment.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Disable HTTP/2 connection coalescing on the proxy appliance for S3 hostnames and force separate outbound connections per host.
- As a short-term fix, we advised enabling application-level retry of shard-range requests with exponential backoff; this reduces failures but does not fix integrity mismatches.

Next steps (in-progress):
- Engage customer network team to collect full proxy request logs and tcpdump for N hours to capture an instance.
- Reproduce in an isolated staging VPC with a mirror proxy appliance (requesting a loaned appliance image from customer).
- Add a heuristic to artifact-service: detect presigned path canonicalization mismatches and switch to single-host ephemeral connections for the remainder of the shard download.
- Create an SRE runbook entry for detecting path-normalization-induced presigned failures.

Attachments/links:
- pcap snippets and header diffs uploaded to support case storage (link in comments).
investigation:
2026-03-10: Support validated customer traces and pcap: mismatch found between sent and forwarded request-target; reproducer script created.
2026-03-11: Eng (edge-proxy) confirmed certain proxy firmware versions perform aggressive path normalization when H2 coalescing is enabled. Identified candidate mitigation to avoid coalescing for hosts with presigned URLs.
2026-03-12: Devs instrumented artifact-service to detect path rewraps and fall back to non-coalesced fetch; initial internal QA started.
resolution: Mitigation in progress: artifact-service will be patched to detect presigned path mismatches and open a dedicated HTTP/1.1 or non-coalesced HTTP/2 connection for the affected host. Customer applied recommended workaround (disable coalescing) and reported immediate reduction in failures. Full patch targeted for 2026-03-22; post-deploy we will coordinate with customer to re-enable coalescing in controlled canary.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Leah Kim (Support): Received case from BlueWave. Initial triage showed signature mismatch in S3 logs. Asked customer to capture tcpdump at egress appliance.
2026-03-10 - BlueWave NetOps (Customer): Uploaded tcpdump and proxy logs: see s3-proxy-pcap-20260310.tar.gz. Noted that turning off coalescing reduced the error rate notably.
2026-03-11 - Rajesh Patel (SRE): Confirmed proxy path rewriting visible in pcap. Opening internal ticket with edge-proxy team. Tagging @edge-proxy for input.

2026-03-11 - Edge Proxy Team (comment): Firmware v5.4 has an option 'normalize-uri' when coalescing hosts. Default behavior attempts to dedupe slashes which can break presigned canonicalization. Recommend disabling for S3 hostnames.
2026-03-12 - Leah Kim (Support): Customer applied workaround and reported 95% reduction in errors. Continuing to validate integrity for long-running downloads.
2026-03-12 - Rajesh Patel (SRE): Patch PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/artifact-service/pull/1187 (adds detection and non-coalesced fallback). QA started.
